Fable agent agrees with the direction, recommending annotating the slow accessor with @available(*, unavailable) via a post-process script rather than forking flatc, and surfaced a gap where most generated Swift files lack a reproducible regen path.

Explains that @available(*, unavailable) is a Swift compiler attribute that makes a symbol impossible to reference, producing a hard compile error with a custom message—stronger than a deprecation warning.
and why do we need to put that?
Explains the annotation prevents the same performance bug from recurring by making misuse a compile error, since the bad call site looks idiomatic and the failure mode is silent and delayed.

Clarifies the O(n) copy is legitimate since the payload needs independent ownership, and the bug was the constant factor (per-byte vs bulk copy). Notes a potential real symptom: eager copying of all projections regardless of whether they're consumed.
